title: reconsider examines the rule's decisions in the order it took them
line: two census pages, the owner accepting a son on the 1920 page: one run of reconsider takes the 1940 father on that, then in its next pass the 1940 son, the first card of his page, on his father's decision, both within one second of the clock; a second run examines the father before the son, though the son's card is the older, keeps both, takes nothing and writes nothing

steps.say: the 1920 census page, a household with a son Frederick M among the children: nobody on it is accepted, so the rule takes nobody
the 1940 census page, a household with a father Frederick and a son Frederick, the son's card the first of the page and so the oldest
the owner accepts Frederick M on the 1920 page: his name and birth year rest on a trusted source, and nothing else is taken yet

expect.why: the other four of the 1920 page wait
the 1940 page waits: none of it is taken by the decision itself

steps.say: reconsider within one second of the clock: the 1940 father agrees with the accepted name and birth year and is taken first; the 1940 son, a card older than his father's, is taken in the next pass, on his father's decision

expect.why: the same second as his father's: the decided-at column cannot tell which was taken first
the mother and the sister wait for the owner

steps.say: reconsider again: the father, taken first, is examined first, so the son's ground holds his father's decision; both kept, nothing taken, nothing written

expect.why: the first decision examined is the father's, though the son's card is the older
a run that changes nothing writes nothing
